blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

faq.q: Which schools are in Panorama Ridge?
faq.a: Panorama Ridge Secondary (13220 64 Ave) and Colebrook Elementary (5404 125a St) are in the area, with McLeod Road Traditional (6325 142 St) also serving it; catchments are by address via the SD36 School Locator.

Buses on the 132 St / 64 Ave and 152 St corridors (routes 321, 322, 324) link the area to Newton Exchange and Surrey Central Station, and the R1 RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard west of the area.

faq.q: What governs land use here now?
faq.a: The South Newton NCP was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update, so the OCP and Zoning Bylaw 12000 govern; a lot's zoning can be checked in City mapping.

faq.q: Can a house add a suite or more units?
faq.a: Surrey's SSMUH rules allow one secondary suite in a house and 3–4 units on most single-family/duplex lots by size band, subject to the zone and servicing.

faq.q: Are there creeks or floodplain in the area?
faq.a: The plan area includes fish-bearing creeks (Archibald Creek headwaters, Sullivan Heights Creek), so riparian rules can affect creek-side lots, and the Serpentine lowlands lie south of Highway 10.
